decision: Widen SAFE_FREEFORM to permit # (and verify @ for email-style refs?). Plan assumed canonical values like 'Closes #{issue}' would parse — they will not. Schema must accept # before Task 1.1.3 seed succeeds.
alternatives: Strip # from canonical values (changes luca-framework convention)
Add only # (keep most of allowlist tight)
reasoning: Plan task 1.1.3 explicitly stores 'Closes #' and 'Closes #{issue}' values. SAFE_FREEFORM /^[\w \t{}/,.():\-]*$/ rejects #. Without this widening, the seed call will fail Zod validation. Adding # is the minimal fix; security review at PR time can validate prompt-injection surface.
risk: If # enables prompt-injection vector (e.g. agent instruction-channel hijack), widening surface. Mitigated: # is not a control char; values still capped at 64 chars; SAFE_FREEFORM still rejects quotes/backticks/newlines/shell-metas. Worst case is a rendered string contains '#' literal — bounded.
reviewHint: Verify SAFE_FREEFORM widening to permit # does not enable any prompt-injection vector that the original allowlist closed. Original commit message claimed 'closes the newline-injection vector' — check that # is not similarly load-bearing.
